newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian consumers plan on shopping spree - survey.
newsitem.headline: Canadian consumers plan on shopping spree - survey.

text.p: Canadian consumers feel the recent trend of declining interest rates has ended and that it is time to dust off their wallets, said a quarterly study by the Conference Board of Canada released on Thursday.

The board's winter index of consumer attitudes jumped 2.3 points to 104.6 from an adjusted third-quarter level of 102.3, while the business confidence index reached an all-time high of 153.1, the board said.
"Consumers think interest rates have hit bottom, so they are ready as ever to buy big-ticket items," said Paul Darby, the board's director of economic services.

The level of respondents who believed that now was a good time to make a major purchase jumped to 58 percent, the highest since 1987 and an increase of 9.4 points from three months ago, the board said.
"This is good news for retailers," Darby said.
All regions except British Columbia posted an increase in consumer confidence, with the three Prairie provinces enjoying the largest jump at 14.5 points, the board said.
Consumer confidence in Quebec rose a mere 0.7 of a point due to continued expectations of a poor job market in the economically strapped province, the board said.
Confidence in British Columbia fell by 0.1 point.
The good consumer news was tempered by continued financial pessimism on the part of business.

The percentage of business respondents who believed their financial positions would improve fell to 53.4 percent from 65.4 percent, while those who expected their financial position to worsen rose to 6.1 percent from 5.8 percent, the board said.
Both surveys were taken last December.
